video_title: Bitcoin Is Coming for the $12T Repo Market
gist: David 'Bitcoin Dave' Seroy of Alpen Labs argues Bitcoin's next step-function of value comes not from more treasury-company buying but from rebuilding the repo/credit market onchain, where a Morpho-vault LP token backed exclusively by fixed-duration Bitcoin-collateralized loans (a 'Bitcoin CLO') becomes the pristine collateral that captures exorbitant privilege. He details the BitVM1-to-BitVM3 (garbled circuits) research arc that lets a trust-minimized ZK rollup exist on Bitcoin without a soft fork, targets Alpen mainnet in the fall, and names Base, Arc and Tempo — not other Bitcoin L2s — as the real competition. Note: the transcript never states a '$12T' repo figure despite the title.

themes.theme: Bitcoin's next step function is not guaranteed

insights.claim: Bitcoin has stepped up in adoption, legitimacy and price each cycle (2017-18 retail plus Galaxy's founding, 2020-21 Michael Sailor's treasury model, and now the push from digital gold to digital capital), but the host argues no future step function is guaranteed simply because prior ones happened.
insights.speaker: host (Bankless)
insights.so_what: Frames Bitcoin's next leg as narrative- and infrastructure-dependent rather than automatic; investors should look for the specific mechanism that drives the next re-rating rather than extrapolating past cycles.
insights.quote: The next step function increase in Bitcoin is not guaranteed even though it seemingly has done very very well previously.

insights.claim: Institutional participation in Bitcoin arrived primarily as volatility suppression rather than as directional buying, which mutes the price craziness that historically drove Bitcoin's memetic adoption.
insights.speaker: David 'Bitcoin Dave' Seroy (Alpen Labs)
insights.so_what: Implies structurally lower realized volatility and weaker retail-attention flywheels; bearish for vol-selling premium and for narratives that rely on parabolic moves to recruit new holders.
insights.quote: And so institutions are here, but they are volatility suppression machines.

insights.claim: The sovereign debt crisis and an eventual strong phase of monetary debasement are the core macro driver for Bitcoin, and AI productivity gains are unlikely to fully bail governments out of that crisis.
insights.speaker: David 'Bitcoin Dave' Seroy (Alpen Labs)
insights.so_what: Positions Bitcoin as the primary debasement hedge and explicitly rejects the 'AI-driven growth solves the deficit' counterargument that would undercut the trade.
insights.quote: I do think that you know eventually we will hit a kind of strong phase of monetary debasement. I'm not sure that AI is going to entirely bail us out of of of that crisis and I do think Bitcoin is in prime position and arguably sole position to to capitalize

insights.claim: Bitcoin's ultimate market capture may be capped by its own protocol limitations, and adding trustless computation via expressive layer 2s is what would lift that cap beyond 'non-sovereign store of value'.
insights.speaker: David 'Bitcoin Dave' Seroy (Alpen Labs)
insights.so_what: Sets up programmability, not accumulation, as the marginal value driver for BTC — a different investable surface than treasury-company equity.

insights.claim: Bitcoin's original steward class of 'high priests' is aging out and the protocol now has competing constituencies (privacy, money, anti-data), so its future technical direction is unresolved and may fork into multiple directions.
insights.speaker: David 'Bitcoin Dave' Seroy (Alpen Labs)
insights.so_what: Governance ambiguity raises the value of designs that ship without a soft fork and lowers the odds of any consensus-change-dependent thesis.
insights.quote: And I think the core narrative that everyone aligns on is Bitcoin is money. But beyond that, there are kind of a lot of people that are kind of vying for their vision of Bitcoin.

themes.theme: Talent drain and crypto's product-market-fit crisis

insights.claim: A decade-plus cohort of crypto evangelists is burning out and moving on while young talent routes to AI instead of crypto, leaving leadership positions unreplaced across the industry.
insights.speaker: host (Bankless)
insights.so_what: A talent-supply headwind is a slow-moving negative for the pace of crypto innovation and a reason to underwrite fewer, more focused teams.
insights.quote: At the same time that that's happening, uh crypto is just not cool. And so, all young talent is going into AI and we're not actually replacing some of the leadership in talent.

insights.claim: The talent exodus is a genuine crisis for broader crypto because many use cases lack product-market fit and token narratives routinely drop 99%, but it is materially less severe in Bitcoin where builders are anchored by the monetary and debasement thesis.
insights.speaker: David 'Bitcoin Dave' Seroy (Alpen Labs)
insights.so_what: Argues for relative allocation toward Bitcoin-native infrastructure over generalized alt-L1/app token exposure during a talent downcycle.
insights.quote: there's like no product market fit and people are like why am I wasting time on this like you know like you just go after these token narratives and they drop 99%

insights.claim: Bitcoin's true-believer base is comfortable holding through a sideways 'crab' market, which provides a stable ownership floor even when broader crypto sentiment is depressed.
insights.speaker: David 'Bitcoin Dave' Seroy (Alpen Labs)
insights.so_what: Supports the case that BTC drawdowns are absorbed by low-turnover holders, keeping float tight during risk-off periods.

themes.theme: BitVM research arc: trust-minimized Bitcoin bridges without a soft fork

insights.claim: Bitcoin's 2020 Taproot upgrade unintentionally enabled arbitrary data embedding, which spawned both JPEG inscriptions on layer 1 and the research papers proposing rollups and ZK rollups on Bitcoin.
insights.speaker: David 'Bitcoin Dave' Seroy (Alpen Labs)
insights.so_what: The entire Bitcoin L2 investment category traces to a side effect of the last soft fork, meaning no further consensus change is required for the thesis to play out.

insights.claim: BitVM, introduced by Robin Linus, brings a weaker form of ZK verification to Bitcoin with no soft fork by replacing threshold multisig bridge security with a 1-of-n honest-operator assumption.
insights.speaker: David 'Bitcoin Dave' Seroy (Alpen Labs)
insights.so_what: The security model is the key diligence question for any Bitcoin bridge: 1-of-n honest is strictly stronger than 6-of-10 threshold custody used by wrapped BTC products.
insights.quote: even if nine of those are malicious, as long as there's one single honest operator in that multisig, then the funds are cryptographically secure

insights.claim: The BitVM trade-off curve improved from months-long ZK verification in BitVM1, to roughly two weeks with very high onchain costs in BitVM2, to BitVM3 garbled circuits which move computation offchain at the cost of larger offchain data storage.
insights.speaker: David 'Bitcoin Dave' Seroy (Alpen Labs)
insights.so_what: Quantifies why earlier Bitcoin L2 attempts were economically unusable and why the current generation is the first that could carry institutional-size flows.
insights.quote: this is not going to you're not going to be required to spend $200,000 in a block to, you know, perform ZK verification and you're not going to have to wait 6 months to bridge out your funds

insights.claim: Only one live ZK rollup exists on Bitcoin today and it uses a BitVM2-style bridge with material trade-offs and, by the speaker's read of its block explorer, very little activity; the industry is shifting to the BitVM3 garbled-circuits family.
insights.speaker: David 'Bitcoin Dave' Seroy (Alpen Labs)
insights.so_what: Live-on-mainnet is not the same as traction; on-chain activity, not launch announcements, is the metric to track for Bitcoin L2s.

insights.claim: A newer cryptography line — the 'pipes v2' paper bringing witness encryption to Bitcoin without a soft fork — could enable covenants and native ZK verification, making further capability gains a matter of engineering rather than consensus change.
insights.speaker: David 'Bitcoin Dave' Seroy (Alpen Labs)
insights.so_what: If covenants can arrive without a fork, the long-stalled Bitcoin soft-fork debate stops being the gating risk for Bitcoin DeFi buildout.
insights.quote: whether it's BBM3 an iteration of that or down the line this very sexy cryptography like I'm quite confident that all of this is coming to Bitcoin

insights.claim: Because the current designs need no soft fork, Bitcoin L2 teams have escaped years of public governance fighting and shifted entirely to shipping, which the speaker cites as the reason builder morale in his corner is at an all-time high despite depressed industry vibes.
insights.speaker: David 'Bitcoin Dave' Seroy (Alpen Labs)
insights.so_what: Removes political risk from the build timeline, so execution risk is the remaining variable to underwrite.
insights.quote: Like, we're just building every day. We can do this without a soft fork.

themes.theme: What a Bitcoin ZK rollup actually looks like

insights.claim: Alpen's Bitcoin layer 2 is architected to look like an Ethereum rollup such as Optimism or Arbitrum, with an EVM execution environment as the headline product rather than a copy of Bitcoin's layer 1.
insights.speaker: David 'Bitcoin Dave' Seroy (Alpen Labs)
insights.so_what: Bitcoin L2 tooling and developer surface converge on EVM standards, lowering integration cost for existing DeFi protocols to deploy there.

insights.claim: Beneath the Alpen EVM sits an unannounced permissionless middleware bridge layer called Strata, modeled on Celestia's ZK accounts, which can settle proofs from multiple execution domains and pipe BTC to Ethereum, Solana or custom environments.
insights.speaker: David 'Bitcoin Dave' Seroy (Alpen Labs)
insights.so_what: Reframes the product from 'another Bitcoin L2' to a bridge standard whose value accrues from BTC routed across chains, a much larger addressable surface.

insights.claim: Even in a multi-execution-environment design where any chain that can produce a zero-knowledge proof can settle, the EVM is expected to remain the dominant execution environment in practice.
insights.speaker: David 'Bitcoin Dave' Seroy (Alpen Labs)
insights.so_what: Argues against paying up for exotic VM ecosystems; EVM liquidity gravity persists even on Bitcoin-anchored infrastructure.

themes.theme: Repo and exorbitant privilege as the real prize

insights.claim: The repo market is where the vast majority of the world's wealth and dollars actually sit, and whichever asset anchors repo collateral captures the true exorbitant privilege — which is why rebuilding repo onchain is a bigger lever on Bitcoin's value than more corporate treasury buying.
insights.speaker: David 'Bitcoin Dave' Seroy (Alpen Labs)
insights.so_what: Redirects the bull case for BTC from flow-based accumulation stories to collateral-status capture, a far larger and more durable pool of demand.
insights.quote: And whoever anchors repo, that that is the true exorbitant privilege.

insights.claim: Offshore shadow banks can create dollar credit with effectively no reserve requirements, but must eventually settle it through repo by posting pristine collateral, so all that shadow credit squeezes through a narrow collateral door.
insights.speaker: David 'Bitcoin Dave' Seroy (Alpen Labs)
insights.so_what: Explains the structural, non-discretionary bid for whatever asset is accepted as repo collateral — the demand channel any onchain challenger must replicate.
insights.quote: there's you imagine huge amounts of liabilities and credit that's created in the shadow banking system that has to squeeze through this tiny door of repo in order to to to to settle

insights.claim: Mortgage-backed securities served as major repo collateral before 2008, and the resulting collateral scarcity and rehypothecation pushed MBS prices up and interest rates down, which is why rates were so low going into the great financial crisis; that privilege has since transferred to US Treasuries and the US government.
insights.speaker: David 'Bitcoin Dave' Seroy (Alpen Labs)
insights.so_what: Historical precedent that collateral status, not fundamentals, drove an entire asset class's valuation — the template for what Bitcoin-backed collateral could do.
insights.quote: People said they're starving for collateral because they need more settlement for the the the the shadow banking system that pushes the price of mortgage back securities up which pushes the interest rates down.

insights.claim: Recreating repo onchain requires three distinct components: a collateral asset, a borrowing and lending engine such as Morpho or Fluid, and a settlement asset which will be treasury-backed stablecoins standing in for bank reserves.
insights.speaker: David 'Bitcoin Dave' Seroy (Alpen Labs)
insights.so_what: A clean three-slot map for where value accrues onchain; the collateral slot is described as the still-unclaimed one and therefore the investable gap.

insights.claim: Bitcoin itself cannot be the pristine prime collateral of an onchain repo market because it is volatile — the pristine collateral must be dollar denominated.
insights.speaker: David 'Bitcoin Dave' Seroy (Alpen Labs)
insights.so_what: Kills the naive 'BTC becomes the new Treasury' framing and points instead to dollar instruments backed by BTC loans as the asset to own.
insights.quote: But the question is what is going to be the pristine prime collateral within this onchain repo market and it's not going to be Bitcoin because Bitcoin is volatile, right? It has to be a dollar denominated asset.

insights.claim: The plan is to build a parallel onchain repo market rather than integrate with or replace the existing tradfi repo system, with the speaker explicitly declining to promise displacement of a market of that size.
insights.speaker: David 'Bitcoin Dave' Seroy (Alpen Labs)
insights.so_what: Sets realistic expectations: the near-term opportunity is a new, smaller credit market growing fast, not immediate capture of tradfi repo volumes.
insights.quote: And maybe I I don't want to like over promise here that it's like boom, we're going to replace

insights.claim: Capital will migrate onchain not out of ideological alignment with Bitcoin but because the economics of a Bitcoin-backed repo system will be superior to offchain tradfi economics.
insights.speaker: David 'Bitcoin Dave' Seroy (Alpen Labs)
insights.so_what: Sets a falsifiable test for the thesis: watch whether onchain Bitcoin-backed rates and terms actually beat offchain alternatives.
insights.quote: you will start amassing huge sickening amounts of of capital into Bitcoin. Not because they care about Bitcoin or they're aligned with the values, but simply because the economics for the dollar system are superior.

themes.theme: The Bitcoin CLO: manufacturing onchain pristine collateral

insights.claim: Two Morpho unlocks make the design possible: V2 isolated vaults that accept only Bitcoin as collateral, and Morpho Midnight which adds fixed durations, allowing a USDC vault to lend across variable, 1, 3, 6, 9 and 12 month Bitcoin-backed loans.
insights.speaker: David 'Bitcoin Dave' Seroy (Alpen Labs)
insights.so_what: Duration is the specific new primitive; its rollout is the trigger event for the whole Bitcoin-credit trade and worth tracking directly on Morpho.

insights.claim: The LP receipt token from a duration-laddered, Bitcoin-only Morpho vault is effectively a Bitcoin collateralized loan obligation — a yield-bearing dollar instrument that the speaker calls the single best pristine collateral creatable onchain.
insights.speaker: David 'Bitcoin Dave' Seroy (Alpen Labs)
insights.so_what: Names the specific instrument to watch for; if it gains acceptance as onchain repo collateral, it becomes the base asset of the whole system.
insights.quote: That instrument, that form of collateral in my opinion is the single best and most pristine collateral that can be created onchain period bar none.

insights.claim: Adding duration lets lenders earn roughly 6-9% instead of the roughly 4% variable money-market rate without moving down in collateral quality, breaking DeFi's historical rule that higher yield requires riskier collateral.
insights.speaker: David 'Bitcoin Dave' Seroy (Alpen Labs)
insights.so_what: A 200-500bp yield pickup at equal or better credit quality is the actual magnet for large dollar allocators; verify it empirically as vaults go live.
insights.quote: So instead of just earning like 4% in a you'll probably be earning 6 7 8 9% on these Bitcoin collateralized loan obligations.

insights.claim: The flywheel runs through a classic securitization carry loop: holders post the LP token to a money market, borrow at variable rates against it and re-lend, and the loop's depth compresses Bitcoin borrowing rates while making the trade profitable for dollar lenders.
insights.speaker: David 'Bitcoin Dave' Seroy (Alpen Labs)
insights.so_what: Explains the mechanism by which onchain Bitcoin borrowing rates could fall from ~10% toward tradfi levels — the key competitive weapon.

insights.claim: Collateral quality directly sets loop leverage: risky Bitcoin collateral supports maybe 60% LTV and only about 1.5x looping, while a ZK-rollup-grade, possibly insured Bitcoin gets the highest LTV at the lowest rates.
insights.speaker: David 'Bitcoin Dave' Seroy (Alpen Labs)
insights.so_what: Gives a concrete valuation channel for bridge security: better trust assumptions translate mechanically into higher LTV, more leverage and tighter rates.
insights.quote: maybe we're willing to lend 60% LTV on that, which means you can only get maybe one and a halfx leverage loop

insights.claim: The safety argument for the Bitcoin CLO rests on the claim that Bitcoin-backed loans on major DeFi protocols have taken on bad debt zero times, so the LP token would only break its dollar peg if those loans became undercollateralized.
insights.speaker: David 'Bitcoin Dave' Seroy (Alpen Labs)
insights.so_what: The historical zero-bad-debt track record is the underwriting basis for treating levered loops on this collateral as low risk; it is also the single assumption whose failure breaks the thesis.
insights.quote: The amount of times Bitcoin back loans have taken on bad debt in DeFi and the major protocols like a and morpho, zero.

insights.claim: Tokenized treasuries and RWAs are a weaker basis for onchain repo than Bitcoin-backed loans because they add trust assumptions vulnerable to a single lawsuit or censorship, are hard to build deep markets in, and yield less.
insights.speaker: David 'Bitcoin Dave' Seroy (Alpen Labs)
insights.so_what: A direct bear case against the consensus RWA-collateral trade and a reason to prefer crypto-native collateral rails.
insights.quote: It's like one lawsuit and these things get censored and you know, you're screwed.

insights.claim: Borrowing against Bitcoin is described as one of the few, if not the only, use cases Bitcoin holders actually want, and Bitcoin has consistently been the largest collateral book onchain across BlockFi, Celsius, Morpho, Aave and Maple.
insights.speaker: David 'Bitcoin Dave' Seroy (Alpen Labs)
insights.so_what: Demand-side evidence that the borrower base already exists, which is the scarce ingredient most onchain credit products lack.

insights.claim: Current fixed-maturity Bitcoin-backed borrowing costs run around 10%, compressing toward 9.9% plus origination fees, leaving substantial room for an onchain product to undercut incumbents on rate and terms.
insights.speaker: David 'Bitcoin Dave' Seroy (Alpen Labs)
insights.so_what: A concrete benchmark: track whether onchain Bitcoin-backed borrow rates break meaningfully below 10% as the signal that the disruption is working.
insights.quote: typically it's around like 10% it's starting to compress down a little bit, but even that it's like, you know, it's it's it's maybe 9.9% and there's like origination fees for it

insights.claim: For Bitcoin holders the primary benefit is cheaper borrowing rather than yield; an unlevered Bitcoin yield product built on the carry trade would pay only about 1-3% in dollar terms, with more available only by looping.
insights.speaker: David 'Bitcoin Dave' Seroy (Alpen Labs)
insights.so_what: Tempers expectations for 'Bitcoin yield' products and clarifies that the real value proposition is borrowing cost, not passive income.
insights.quote: it's not non-levered would probably be in that 1 to 3% range

insights.claim: A vicious competition among vault curators is forming over which mix of durations and collateral produces the best pristine collateral, because whoever's LP token is accepted as pristine captures the exorbitant privilege.
insights.speaker: David 'Bitcoin Dave' Seroy (Alpen Labs)
insights.so_what: Vault curation becomes a winner-take-most business worth watching for concentration and for which curator's receipt token gets rehypothecated most widely.
insights.quote: if your collateral is seen as the pristine collateral Then you win everything

themes.theme: Onchain Bitcoin credit versus Sailor's perpetual preferreds

insights.claim: The Bitcoin CLO is a direct competitor to Michael Sailor's STRC: both take dollars from fixed-income buyers seeking Bitcoin-linked yield, but STRC holders are quasi-backed by Sailor's balance sheet while CLO holders are provably backed by overcollateralized Bitcoin loans.
insights.speaker: David 'Bitcoin Dave' Seroy (Alpen Labs)
insights.so_what: Frames a head-to-head between corporate-credit and onchain-collateral routes to Bitcoin-backed fixed income; relative spreads between the two are the trade.

insights.claim: STRC broke its peg and trades around 85 cents on the dollar because holders levered it in a looping strategy — borrowing at ~4% against a ~10% instrument — and the unwind created massive sell pressure, a fragility the speaker predicted in advance.
insights.speaker: David 'Bitcoin Dave' Seroy (Alpen Labs)
insights.so_what: A live case study in reflexive unwind risk for Bitcoin-linked fixed income; a Bitcoin CLO's resilience against the same dynamic is the key thing to stress test.
insights.quote: when that trade needs to unwind, there becomes massive sell pressure on STRC and it starts to break peg, which is where it's now at at like you know 85 cents on the dollar

insights.claim: Bitcoin ascending from digital gold to digital credit is the better narrative for the asset's next step function, and the fact that Sailor, Strive and Semler are all pursuing perpetual-preferred structures suggests real demand for Bitcoin-backed credit rather than one man's dream.
insights.speaker: host (Bankless)
insights.so_what: Multiple independent issuers pursuing the same structure is corroborating evidence for the Bitcoin-as-credit theme regardless of which venue wins.
insights.quote: I do like Bitcoin as digital credit as the better meme for Bitcoin

insights.claim: Bitcoin's investable role in this framework is as the lowest-counterparty-risk collateral, filling the same slot that mortgage-backed securities occupied before 2008 and Treasuries occupy today, which is why dollars will be lent against it.
insights.speaker: David 'Bitcoin Dave' Seroy (Alpen Labs)
insights.so_what: Reframes BTC's bull case around counterparty risk rather than scarcity, a lens that also explains why onchain issuance beats issuer-dependent structures like STRC.

themes.theme: Alpen Labs' competitive position and timeline

insights.claim: Alpen Labs expects to be live on mainnet in the fall, with the Alpen EVM as the user-facing chain and the unannounced Strata layer as an open bridge standard beneath it.
insights.speaker: David 'Bitcoin Dave' Seroy (Alpen Labs)
insights.so_what: A dated catalyst for the Bitcoin ZK rollup category, with the usual soft-TM caveat on crypto launch dates.
insights.quote: we'll probably be live on mainet in fall or you know soon TM

insights.claim: Prior Bitcoin L2s failed not only on technology but because they never closed the big fish — tier-one DeFi and stablecoin teams like Circle, Tether, Morpho and Fluid must be won through a brutal BD process, not summoned by Bitcoin branding.
insights.speaker: David 'Bitcoin Dave' Seroy (Alpen Labs)
insights.so_what: Distribution and protocol partnerships, not cryptography, are the diligence variable that separates surviving Bitcoin L2s from the graveyard.
insights.quote: none of the other Bitcoin L2s they didn't close the big fish is really what it came down to

insights.claim: The competitive set for a Bitcoin L2 is not other Bitcoin L2s — Botanix wound down its chain and the one live BitVM2-based competitor shows little activity — but Base, Arc and Tempo, which host wrapped Bitcoin.
insights.speaker: David 'Bitcoin Dave' Seroy (Alpen Labs)
insights.so_what: Redefines the market map: BTC-denominated DeFi share, not Bitcoin-L2 share, is the metric, and Base is the incumbent to beat.
insights.quote: I think our real competition honestly is is bass and arc and tempo

insights.claim: Circle has announced a tokenized Bitcoin product deploying on Ethereum and Arc, extending the wrapped-BTC competitive front to a major stablecoin issuer.
insights.speaker: David 'Bitcoin Dave' Seroy (Alpen Labs)
insights.so_what: A regulated issuer entering tokenized BTC directly threatens the trust-minimized bridge pitch by offering distribution incumbents will find easier to adopt.

insights.claim: The strategy to outcompete wrapped and custodial BTC products such as cbBTC and WBTC pairs ZK rollup cryptography with institutional-level insurance on the bridge, since technical purity alone is only a bonus point and the pitch must win on economics.
insights.speaker: David 'Bitcoin Dave' Seroy (Alpen Labs)
insights.so_what: Bridge insurance is the underrated unlock for institutional Bitcoin DeFi; its availability and pricing is a concrete thing to watch.
insights.quote: it can't just be on the technical purity. That's just like a bonus point. It has to be on the actual economics.

insights.claim: The go-to-market plan copies Morpho's Coinbase playbook — pursue a distribution partner that acts as kingmaker rather than chasing organic developer adoption.
insights.speaker: David 'Bitcoin Dave' Seroy (Alpen Labs)
insights.so_what: Watch for a large-distribution partner announcement as the single highest-signal event for whether this Bitcoin credit market gets real volume.
insights.quote: I think if you look at the model that Moro laid out with Coinbase Coinbase was essentially a kingmaker for them

insights.claim: Alpen is deliberately an opinionated app-chain for Bitcoin credit rather than an open developer ecosystem, declining grants and hackathons because it cannot outcompete chains like MegaETH on general-purpose use cases.
insights.speaker: David 'Bitcoin Dave' Seroy (Alpen Labs)
insights.so_what: A focused single-use-case chain is a different investment profile than an ecosystem play — judge it on Bitcoin-backed loan volume, not developer counts.

insights.claim: By the same logic, the Ethereum layer 1 should be run as an app chain for Ether the asset with all applications serving ETH as pristine collateral, which would do more for ETH's value than the open world-computer framing.
insights.speaker: David 'Bitcoin Dave' Seroy (Alpen Labs)
insights.so_what: A pointed critique of Ethereum's value-accrual narrative from a former ETH advocate; relevant to any ETH thesis that depends on ecosystem breadth rather than collateral status.
insights.quote: the Ethereum layer 1 is an app chain for Ether the asset. It's the pristine collateral on the Ethereum layer 1. All applications should serve Ether the asset.

insights.claim: Morpho Midnight is rolling out in phases starting on Ethereum, and early fixed maturities are expected to be short — around one or two months — so a full 12-month Bitcoin CLO curve will take time rather than appearing immediately.
insights.speaker: David 'Bitcoin Dave' Seroy (Alpen Labs)
insights.so_what: Paces the trade: the yield curve builds from the short end, so watch maturity extension as the progress indicator rather than expecting a step change.
insights.quote: the maturities are going to start off small like you know a month or two is my intuition

insights.claim: The speaker expects duration-enabled lending to show up first on Ethereum the network but not with ETH as the collateral asset, because Morpho's lending volume is concentrated in cbBTC on Base rather than in Ethereum layer 1 markets.
insights.speaker: David 'Bitcoin Dave' Seroy (Alpen Labs)
insights.so_what: Points at cbBTC-on-Base Morpho markets as the leading indicator where the Bitcoin-CLO structure will first prove out or fail.
insights.quote: Morpho is first and foremost only blowing out with CBTC on base
